Adopt int8 quantization for the reranker. Rationale: dynamic QInt8 quantization cut the reranker from 91MB fp32 to 22MB with no measurable Recall@1 regression on the golden set, and Xenova publishes no fp32-only alternative worth the extra disk.

Reject Dolt's native vector index for M0. Rationale: the vector index feature is explicitly alpha upstream ("too slow for us to recommend using it in production"), and brute-force cosine over a 10^3-10^4 row corpus is fast enough that the alpha risk buys nothing yet.

Keep embeddings out of the Dolt repo. Rationale: fp32 blobs defeat prolly-tree structural sharing, so every edited fact would append irreversible history; a derived side-store SQLite file can be rebuilt from source text instead.

Choose ULID over UUIDv4 for primary keys. Rationale: ULIDs sort lexicographically by creation time, which keeps Dolt's prolly-tree insert pattern append-mostly instead of randomly scattering across the key space.

Port memhub's pipeline with the storage swapped underneath.
Same models, same fusion, same knobs, same eval harness.
Lexical gather runs per-source-type full-text search, limit 50 per type.
Vector gather brute-forces cosine over the embedding side-store.
Fusion blends 0.5 lexical and 0.5 cosine, then applies age decay and penalties.
Rerank runs the int8 cross-encoder over the top-20 pool before truncating to 6 results.

The MCP server owns the store for the life of the process.
Every CLI invocation is a separate process, so it cannot hold the lock itself.
Instead it probes for a live owner over the loopback endpoint and routes
every store operation through that owner's IPC surface.
If no owner is listening, the CLI takes the lock itself and becomes the owner
for the duration of that one command.

embeddings.sqlite is a derived side-store, never versioned and never synced.
Its schema is (source_type, source_id, model_name) mapping to a vector BLOB,
a content hash, and a dimension.
A fresh clone needs one index build pass before recall returns results;
the stale_embeddings warning machinery covers the gap in the meantime.

M0 is a spike, not a feature milestone: its only job is go/no-go.
Four rigs run in parallel: the embedded-driver concurrency soak, the
ONNX-in-Go parity check, the retrieval golden-set gate, and the hub
round-trip over Tailscale.
A fail on any of them stops the project and gets written up rather than
quietly worked around.

Rig 1 ran five configurations against the embedded driver.
Across 121,180 acknowledged writes, zero were lost, corrupted, or invisible
to a concurrent reader after an unclean kill and stale-lock recovery.
The negative control confirmed the reconciler actually detects the failure
modes it claims to detect, rather than reporting zero because it never looked.
